name: CTET Paper 2 (Maths & Science)
fullName: Central Teacher Eligibility Test – Paper II (Elementary Stage, Classes VI–VIII), Mathematics & Science stream
frequency: Usually twice a year (sessions are sometimes skipped or shifted)
approxCandidates: ≈18.7 lakh appeared for Paper 2, both streams combined, in the Feb 2026 session (Papers 1 + 2 together: 26.5 lakh registered, 23.2 lakh appeared)
eligibility: Graduation (50%) plus B.Ed, or Graduation plus a 2-year D.El.Ed, or a 4-year integrated B.A./B.Sc.Ed or B.El.Ed (final-year students may apply), as per NCTE norms. No upper age limit, and the certificate is valid for life.

notification.summary: The September 2026 (22nd) CTET was notified by CBSE around 11 May 2026 and scheduled in offline OMR mode on 6 Sep 2026. Applications are closed and the result is awaited. In the Feb 2026 session, Paper 2 had a pass rate of only 18.56% (3.47 lakh qualified); the result was declared on 30–31 Mar 2026. The next cycle's notification is expected around Nov–Dec 2026. Dates come from news reports found by web search on 2026-10-10, because ctet.nic.in could not be reached from the research sandbox. Verify on the official site.
notification.source: https://ctet.nic.in (official), cross-checked with the CBSE Feb 2026 result notice https://www.cbse.gov.in/cbsenew/documents/PUBLIC_%20NOTICE_CTET_Feb_2026_RESULT_31032026.pdf and Careers360/PW news reports

pattern.notes: Real paper: 150 MCQs of 1 mark each, no negative marking, 2½ hours. Qualifying marks are 60% (90/150) for General and 55% (82/150) for SC/ST/OBC/PwD. Officially, 'Mathematics & Science' is a single 60-question section (30 Maths + 30 Science). It is split into two sections here only for analysis. Within each subject, about 20 questions test content (NCERT Classes VI–VIII) and 10 test pedagogy. This mock uses English as Language I and Hindi as Language II, and the languages must differ. The question bank holds 60 original questions (CDP 12, English 10, Hindi 8, Maths 15, Science 15), so a mock built from it is a scaled-down version of the full paper.

trendAnalysis.summary: This analysis covers the Jul 2024, Dec 2024 and Feb 2026 sessions. No CTET exam was held in calendar 2025: the Dec-2025 cycle was conducted on 8 Feb 2026. Paper 2 is consistently tougher than Paper 1, with only 18.56% passing in Feb 2026. The Maths & Science section is the most time-consuming: Maths content leans on geometry (angles, triangles, polygons, symmetry), integers/fractions and simple algebra, while Science content is drawn from NCERT Class VI–VIII topics (materials, the living world, electricity & magnets, light). Pedagogy questions now use classroom scenarios, for example van Hiele levels, error analysis, inquiry-based science and process skills. CDP for Paper 2 emphasises adolescence, Kohlberg, inclusive education (RPwD Act 2016) and NEP-2020 aligned assessment.

resources.notes: CBSE does not keep a public archive of CTET question papers. After each exam it posts the provisional answer key together with each candidate's scanned OMR sheet and question-paper set under 'Candidate Activity' on ctet.nic.in for a short challenge window. Final keys and result notices are published on ctet.nic.in and cbse.gov.in. Full past papers in circulation are reconstructions by coaching publishers, not official copies.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of intrinsic motivation?
options: A student studies hard to win a cash prize
A student solves extra puzzles because she enjoys the challenge
A student revises only because marks will be displayed on the notice board
A student completes homework to avoid a scolding
questions.explanation: Intrinsic motivation comes from interest or enjoyment in the task itself. Prizes, avoiding punishment and public recognition are all external (extrinsic) motivators.

questions.question: According to Vygotsky, children talking aloud to themselves while solving a problem ('private speech'):
options: Should be strictly discouraged in class
Is a sign of a speech disorder
Shows cognitive immaturity and serves no purpose
Helps them guide and regulate their own thinking
questions.explanation: Vygotsky saw private speech as a tool for self-regulation that gradually becomes inner speech. Piaget, by contrast, considered egocentric speech to be non-functional.

questions.question: A 13-year-old can reason, "If all metals conduct electricity and X is a metal, then X conducts electricity," and can systematically test hypotheses. According to Piaget, she is in the:
questions.explanation: Abstract, hypothetico-deductive reasoning develops in the formal operational stage (about 11 years onwards).

questions.question: An adolescent says, "We must obey traffic rules because society would collapse into chaos if everyone ignored laws." According to Kohlberg, this reasoning belongs to the:
questions.explanation: Upholding laws to maintain social order is Stage 4 (conventional level). Stage 5 (social contract) sees laws as agreements that can be changed for the greater good.

questions.question: Which statement best describes adolescence?
options: It is marked by a decline in abstract thinking
It is a period of stable and unchanging emotions
It is a period of rapid physical change and a search for identity
It is marked by complete dependence on parents for decisions
questions.explanation: Adolescence brings puberty-related physical changes and, as Erikson described, the crisis of identity versus role confusion.

questions.question: Which is considered the primary agent of socialisation for a child?
questions.explanation: The family is the first and primary agent of socialisation. School, peers and media are secondary agents.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a component of Robert Sternberg's triarchic theory of intelligence?
questions.explanation: Sternberg's three components are analytical (componential), creative (experiential) and practical (contextual). Emotional intelligence was popularised by Salovey, Mayer and Goleman.

questions.question: In school-based assessment, a portfolio is:
options: A purposeful collection of a learner's work over time that shows progress
A list of marks arranged in rank order
A record of a learner's attendance
questions.explanation: Portfolios collect samples of a student's work over time and support assessment of growth and reflection.

questions.topic: Inclusive Education & Children with Special Needs
questions.question: Which strategy is most helpful for a student with Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD)?
options: Give long assignments to keep the student busy
Break tasks into short steps with clear instructions and frequent feedback
Allow no movement or breaks at all
Seat the student near the door and windows
questions.explanation: Short, structured tasks with immediate feedback suit the attention span of learners with ADHD. Seating near distractions makes focusing harder.

questions.topic: Inclusive Education & Children with Special Needs
questions.question: How many types of disabilities are recognised under the Rights of Persons with Disabilities (RPwD) Act, 2016?
questions.explanation: The RPwD Act, 2016 expanded the list of specified disabilities from 7 (in the 1995 Act) to 21.

questions.question: A Class VII science textbook shows only men as scientists. What is the most appropriate response from the teacher?
options: Tell students that science suits boys better
Discuss this with students and introduce examples of women scientists
Ask only girls to read about the scientists
questions.explanation: Questioning gender bias in materials and offering counter-examples builds gender sensitivity.

questions.question: Who emphasised 'learning by doing' and described the school as a miniature society?
questions.explanation: John Dewey, a pioneer of progressive education, advocated experiential learning and schools as democratic miniature societies.

questions.question:
Read the passage and answer.

"Bamboo is often mistaken for a tree, but it is actually a grass – the largest member of the grass family. Some species can grow nearly a metre in a single day, making bamboo one of the fastest-growing plants on Earth. Because it regenerates from its own roots after harvesting, it does not need to be replanted. Builders in north-east India have used it for centuries to make homes, bridges and scaffolding, and today engineers are studying how it might replace steel in low-cost housing. However, untreated bamboo is vulnerable to insects and moisture, so it must be seasoned carefully before use."

According to the passage, bamboo does not need to be replanted because:
options: It regenerates from its own roots after harvesting
Builders reuse the same bamboo for many years
It belongs to the tree family
It is naturally resistant to insects
questions.explanation: The passage states that bamboo 'regenerates from its own roots after harvesting', so it does not need to be replanted.

questions.question:
Read the passage and answer.

"Bamboo is often mistaken for a tree, but it is actually a grass – the largest member of the grass family. Some species can grow nearly a metre in a single day, making bamboo one of the fastest-growing plants on Earth. Because it regenerates from its own roots after harvesting, it does not need to be replanted. Builders in north-east India have used it for centuries to make homes, bridges and scaffolding, and today engineers are studying how it might replace steel in low-cost housing. However, untreated bamboo is vulnerable to insects and moisture, so it must be seasoned carefully before use."

Which of the following is NOT supported by the passage?
options: Bamboo has been used to build bridges
Engineers are studying bamboo as a substitute for steel
Bamboo belongs to the grass family
questions.explanation: The passage says untreated bamboo is vulnerable to moisture, so the claim that it resists moisture contradicts the passage.

questions.question:
Read the passage and answer.

"Bamboo is often mistaken for a tree, but it is actually a grass – the largest member of the grass family. Some species can grow nearly a metre in a single day, making bamboo one of the fastest-growing plants on Earth. Because it regenerates from its own roots after harvesting, it does not need to be replanted. Builders in north-east India have used it for centuries to make homes, bridges and scaffolding, and today engineers are studying how it might replace steel in low-cost housing. However, untreated bamboo is vulnerable to insects and moisture, so it must be seasoned carefully before use."

The word 'vulnerable' in the passage most nearly means:
questions.explanation: Vulnerable means exposed to damage or harm. Untreated bamboo is easily damaged by insects and moisture.

questions.question:
Read the stanza and answer.

"Rain on the tin roof, a drummer at night,
Knocking and rolling till morning's first light;
The frogs in the ditches sing loud as they please,
And the wind tells its secrets in whispers to trees."

In the first line, the rain is called 'a drummer at night'. The figure of speech used is:
questions.explanation: The rain is directly identified with a drummer, without 'like' or 'as', so it is a metaphor.

questions.question:
Read the stanza and answer.

"Rain on the tin roof, a drummer at night,
Knocking and rolling till morning's first light;
The frogs in the ditches sing loud as they please,
And the wind tells its secrets in whispers to trees."

The line 'And the wind tells its secrets in whispers to trees' is an example of:
questions.explanation: The wind is given the human ability to tell secrets and whisper, so the line uses personification.

questions.question: Communicative Language Teaching (CLT) mainly focuses on:
options: Using language for meaningful communication in real-life situations
Translating texts between English and the mother tongue
Achieving grammatical accuracy through drills alone
Memorising rules of grammar and spelling
questions.explanation: CLT treats communicative competence as the goal and uses tasks such as role-plays and information-gap activities.

questions.question: Many Class VII students make subject–verb agreement errors in their written work. What is the most effective remedial approach?
options: Give focused practice in meaningful writing tasks, with feedback and peer editing
Make students copy the rule ten times
Ignore the errors because they will disappear on their own
Deduct marks for every error without explanation
questions.explanation: Remediation works best when the specific error is addressed in context with feedback, rather than through rote copying or punishment.

questions.question: A rubric for assessing students' paragraph writing should mainly include criteria such as:
options: Content, organisation, vocabulary and grammatical accuracy
questions.explanation: A writing rubric should reflect the components of good writing: ideas, organisation, language use and mechanics.

questions.question: Reading a text quickly to get its general idea or gist is called:
questions.explanation: Skimming is fast reading for the gist. Scanning is searching for specific information such as a date or name.

questions.topic: Challenges of Teaching in Multilingual Classrooms
questions.question: 'Language across the curriculum' implies that:
options: Language learning is the responsibility of the language teacher alone
English should be taught only in the English period
Every subject teacher contributes to the development of students' language
Students' home languages should be kept out of school
questions.explanation: Language develops through all subjects, so every teacher plays a part in building language proficiency.

questions.question:
गद्यांश पढ़कर प्रश्न का उत्तर दीजिए।

"पुस्तकें मनुष्य की सच्ची मित्र होती हैं। वे बिना किसी स्वार्थ के हमें ज्ञान देती हैं और कठिन समय में धैर्य बँधाती हैं। एक अच्छी पुस्तक पढ़ते समय हम लेखक के अनुभवों से जुड़ जाते हैं और नए विचारों से परिचित होते हैं। इसलिए विद्यार्थियों में पढ़ने की आदत बचपन से ही विकसित करनी चाहिए।"

गद्यांश के अनुसार पुस्तकें 'सच्ची मित्र' क्यों हैं?
options: क्योंकि वे केवल मनोरंजन करती हैं
क्योंकि वे बिना स्वार्थ के ज्ञान देती हैं
क्योंकि वे परीक्षा में अंक दिलाती हैं
questions.explanation: गद्यांश में कहा गया है कि पुस्तकें 'बिना किसी स्वार्थ के हमें ज्ञान देती हैं', इसलिए वे सच्ची मित्र हैं।

questions.question:
गद्यांश पढ़कर प्रश्न का उत्तर दीजिए।

"पुस्तकें मनुष्य की सच्ची मित्र होती हैं। वे बिना किसी स्वार्थ के हमें ज्ञान देती हैं और कठिन समय में धैर्य बँधाती हैं। एक अच्छी पुस्तक पढ़ते समय हम लेखक के अनुभवों से जुड़ जाते हैं और नए विचारों से परिचित होते हैं। इसलिए विद्यार्थियों में पढ़ने की आदत बचपन से ही विकसित करनी चाहिए।"

'स्वार्थ' शब्द का विलोम है —
questions.explanation: स्वार्थ (अपना हित) का विलोम परमार्थ (दूसरों का हित) है। 'स्वहित' स्वार्थ का समानार्थी है।

questions.question:
गद्यांश पढ़कर प्रश्न का उत्तर दीजिए।

"पुस्तकें मनुष्य की सच्ची मित्र होती हैं। वे बिना किसी स्वार्थ के हमें ज्ञान देती हैं और कठिन समय में धैर्य बँधाती हैं। एक अच्छी पुस्तक पढ़ते समय हम लेखक के अनुभवों से जुड़ जाते हैं और नए विचारों से परिचित होते हैं। इसलिए विद्यार्थियों में पढ़ने की आदत बचपन से ही विकसित करनी चाहिए।"

'पढ़ने की आदत' में 'की' किस कारक का चिह्न है?
questions.explanation: का, के, की संबंध कारक के चिह्न हैं। कर्म का चिह्न 'को' है, करण का 'से/के द्वारा' है, और अपादान का 'से' (अलग होने के अर्थ में) है।

questions.question: 'माता-पिता' में कौन-सा समास है?
questions.explanation: माता-पिता = माता और पिता। दोनों पद प्रधान हैं और 'और' का लोप है, अतः यह द्वंद्व समास है।

questions.question: उच्च प्राथमिक स्तर पर 'सुनने' के कौशल का विकास करने के लिए सबसे उपयुक्त गतिविधि है —
options: कहानी या समाचार सुनाकर उस पर बातचीत और प्रश्न करना
questions.explanation: सुनी हुई सामग्री पर बातचीत और प्रश्नों से ध्यानपूर्वक सुनने और समझने का कौशल विकसित होता है।

questions.question: उच्च प्राथमिक स्तर पर व्याकरण सिखाने का सबसे प्रभावी तरीका है —
options: केवल व्याकरण की पुस्तक के अभ्यास करवाना
भाषा के प्रयोग के संदर्भ में व्याकरण सिखाना
व्याकरण के नियम और परिभाषाएँ रटवाना
व्याकरण को पाठ से अलग, केवल सूत्रों के रूप में पढ़ाना
questions.explanation: व्याकरण संदर्भ में, यानी पाठों और भाषा-प्रयोग के माध्यम से, सिखाने पर अधिक सार्थक और स्थायी होता है।

questions.question: सतत और व्यापक आकलन के संदर्भ में भाषा-आकलन का मुख्य उद्देश्य है —
options: केवल वार्षिक परीक्षा के अंक देना
बच्चों की आपस में तुलना करना
बच्चों को उत्तीर्ण या अनुत्तीर्ण घोषित करना
बच्चों की प्रगति जानकर शिक्षण-प्रक्रिया में सुधार करना
questions.explanation: आकलन का उद्देश्य सीखने में सहायता करना है। उससे मिली जानकारी शिक्षण को बेहतर बनाने में प्रयुक्त होती है।

questions.question: कविता शिक्षण का मुख्य उद्देश्य है —
questions.explanation: कविता शिक्षण का प्रमुख लक्ष्य रसानुभूति, कल्पना और सौंदर्यबोध का विकास है।

questions.question: What is the HCF of 84 and 126?
Find the value of (−12) × (−5) ÷ (−4) + 7.
If 3x − 7 = 2x + 5, what is the value of 2x?
questions.explanation: 3x − 2x = 5 + 7 gives x = 12, so 2x = 24.

questions.question: ₹720 is divided between two friends in the ratio 4 : 5. What is the larger share?
questions.explanation: Total parts = 9 and one part = 720 ÷ 9 = 80. Larger share = 5 × 80 = ₹400.

questions.question: The angles of a triangle are in the ratio 2 : 3 : 4. What is the largest angle?
questions.explanation: The angles are 2k + 3k + 4k = 180°, so k = 20°. Largest angle = 4 × 20° = 80°.

questions.question: What is the measure of each interior angle of a regular hexagon?
questions.explanation: Sum of interior angles = (6 − 2) × 180° = 720°. Each angle = 720° ÷ 6 = 120°.

questions.question: A polyhedron has 8 vertices and 12 edges. How many faces does it have?
questions.explanation: Euler's formula: F + V − E = 2, so F = 2 − 8 + 12 = 6. (A cube is an example.)

questions.question: The parallel sides of a trapezium are 10 cm and 16 cm, and the distance between them is 7 cm. What is its area?
The volume of a cube is 343 cm³. What is its total surface area?
questions.explanation: Edge = ∛343 = 7 cm. Total surface area = 6 × 7² = 294 cm².

questions.question: What is the median of the data 3, 8, 5, 12, 7, 10?
questions.explanation: Arranged in order: 3, 5, 7, 8, 10, 12. With an even count, the median is the mean of the 3rd and 4th values: (7 + 8) ÷ 2 = 7.5.

questions.question: A Class VI student says, "A rectangle has four right angles and opposite sides equal," but insists that a square cannot be a rectangle. According to the van Hiele model, the student is at the level of:
questions.explanation: At the analysis level, learners describe shapes by their properties but do not yet see relationships between classes of shapes. Seeing that a square is a special rectangle needs informal deduction.

questions.question: A student simplifies 3(x + 4) as 3x + 4. The error shows that the student:
options: Has not correctly applied the distributive property
questions.explanation: 3(x + 4) = 3x + 12. The student multiplied only the first term inside the bracket, which is a misapplication of the distributive property.

questions.question: What is the correct sequence of George Pólya's four steps of problem solving?
options: Carry out the plan → Understand the problem → Devise a plan → Look back
Devise a plan → Understand the problem → Look back → Carry out the plan
Understand the problem → Carry out the plan → Devise a plan → Look back
Understand the problem → Devise a plan → Carry out the plan → Look back
questions.explanation: In How to Solve It, Pólya gives the steps as: understand, plan, execute, then review (look back).

questions.question: Using open-ended questions in mathematics assessment mainly helps a teacher to:
options: Assess students' different strategies and reasoning
Make all students reach the same single answer by the same method
questions.explanation: Open-ended tasks allow several approaches or answers and show how students think.

questions.question: In mathematics, deductive reasoning means:
options: Arriving at specific conclusions logically from accepted axioms or general statements
Making a general rule after observing a few examples
Solving problems only by trial and error
questions.explanation: Deduction moves from the general (axioms, theorems) to the specific. Generalising from examples is inductive reasoning.

questions.question: A food sample is tested with a few drops of dilute iodine solution. Which observation confirms the presence of starch?
options: A translucent patch forms on paper
questions.explanation: Iodine turns blue-black with starch. A violet colour with copper sulphate and caustic soda indicates protein, and a translucent patch indicates fat.

questions.question: Which of the following is a chemical change?
questions.explanation: Rusting produces a new substance, iron oxide, so it is a chemical change. The others are physical changes.

questions.question: Turmeric paper turns red when it is dipped in:
questions.explanation: Turmeric is a natural indicator that turns red in basic solutions. Lime water (calcium hydroxide) is basic, lemon juice and vinegar are acidic, and sugar solution is neutral.

questions.question: In which cell organelle does photosynthesis take place?
questions.explanation: Chloroplasts contain chlorophyll and are the site of photosynthesis. Mitochondria are the site of respiration.

questions.question: In human lungs, the exchange of oxygen and carbon dioxide takes place in the:
questions.explanation: Alveoli are tiny air sacs surrounded by capillaries, and gaseous exchange happens across their thin walls.

questions.question: Which of the following diseases is caused by a virus?
questions.explanation: Polio is caused by the poliovirus. Typhoid and tuberculosis are bacterial, and malaria is caused by the protozoan Plasmodium.

questions.question: An electric fuse works on which effect of electric current?
questions.explanation: When too much current flows, the fuse wire heats up and melts, which breaks the circuit.

questions.question: The image formed by a plane mirror is:
options: Real, inverted and of the same size as the object
Virtual, erect and of the same size as the object
questions.explanation: A plane mirror forms a virtual, erect, laterally inverted image of the same size as the object, as far behind the mirror as the object is in front.

questions.question: A car covers 150 km in 2 hours 30 minutes. What is its average speed?
questions.explanation: Speed = distance ÷ time = 150 km ÷ 2.5 h = 60 km/h.

questions.question: Which of the following is an exhaustible natural resource?
questions.explanation: Coal is a fossil fuel that forms over millions of years, so its reserves can be used up. Sunlight, wind and air are inexhaustible.

questions.question: In an inquiry-based science classroom, the teacher should mainly:
options: Give definitions first and ask students to memorise them
Demonstrate every experiment while students copy the results
Encourage students to ask questions, make predictions and test them through investigation
Avoid questions that do not have a single textbook answer
questions.explanation: Inquiry-based learning engages students in questioning, investigating and drawing conclusions from evidence.

questions.question: A student says, "If I give more water to this plant, it will grow taller than the other one." Which science process skill is the student using?
questions.explanation: The student states a testable, tentative explanation of the relationship between two variables. That is a hypothesis.

questions.question: Which statement best describes the nature of scientific knowledge?
options: It is accepted only on the basis of authority
It is tentative and can be revised in the light of new evidence
It is absolute and can never change
It is a fixed collection of facts to be memorised
questions.explanation: Science is a dynamic, evidence-based body of knowledge that is open to revision.

questions.question: Which is the most appropriate way to assess students' practical (laboratory) skills?
options: Observing students as they perform the activity, using a checklist
Checking how neat their practical notebooks look
Asking students to recite the procedure
questions.explanation: Psychomotor skills are best assessed through direct observation of performance against defined criteria.

questions.question: Many students believe that heavier objects always fall faster than lighter ones. What is the most effective way for the teacher to address this misconception?
options: Create cognitive conflict through a demonstration, followed by discussion
Tell students they are wrong and move on
Ask students to memorise the correct statement
Avoid the topic because it confuses students
questions.explanation: Dropping objects of different mass together creates cognitive conflict. When students confront the discrepancy and discuss it, their concepts change.

questions.question: According to Piaget, the ability to reason about abstract and hypothetical situations, such as "What would happen if there were no friction?", develops in the:
questions.explanation: Abstract, hypothetical and systematic (hypothetico-deductive) reasoning appears in the formal operational stage, from about 11–12 years. Concrete operational thinkers reason logically only about concrete situations.

questions.question: Which classroom practice is most consistent with Vygotsky's socio-cultural theory?
options: Waiting until each child is developmentally "ready" before teaching a concept
Drill and practice with rewards for correct answers
Peer tutoring and collaborative tasks in mixed-ability groups
questions.explanation: Vygotsky saw learning as social: interaction with more capable peers or adults within the ZPD leads development. Waiting for readiness reflects a Piagetian reading, and drill with rewards is behaviourist.

questions.question: A student says, "Laws are agreements made by people for the welfare of all; if a law is unjust, it should be changed through democratic means." According to Kohlberg, this reasoning belongs to the:
questions.explanation: Seeing laws as social contracts that can be changed for the common good is Stage 5 (social contract orientation), which is part of the post-conventional level.

questions.question: Carol Gilligan criticised Kohlberg's theory of moral development mainly because it:
options: Gave too much importance to emotions in moral decisions
Was based largely on male participants and overlooked the ethic of care
Studied only children below five years of age
questions.explanation: Kohlberg's original studies were of boys, and his scale rewards justice-based reasoning. Gilligan argued that this undervalues a care-based morality often expressed by women.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about human development is NOT correct?
options: Development stops once a person reaches adolescence
Development involves both qualitative and quantitative changes
The physical, cognitive and social domains of development are interrelated
questions.explanation: Development continues throughout life, from conception to old age. The other three statements are accepted principles of development.

questions.question: A child's development is best described as the result of:
options: The interaction of heredity and environment
Schooling alone, independent of heredity and environment
questions.explanation: Heredity sets potentials and the environment shapes how far and in what way they are realised; the two continually interact.

questions.question: A student easily recognises and classifies plants, birds and rocks and enjoys nature walks. According to Howard Gardner, she shows strength in:
questions.explanation: Naturalistic intelligence is the ability to recognise, classify and understand elements of the natural world.

questions.question: To address individual differences among learners in a Class VII classroom, the teacher should:
options: Pitch every lesson at the level of the average learner
Seat slower learners permanently in a separate group
Use varied tasks, materials and groupings matched to learners' readiness and interests
Give the same homework to all, but make it more difficult
questions.explanation: Differentiated instruction recognises that learners vary in readiness, interests and learning styles. Teaching to the average or permanently segregating learners ignores these differences.

questions.topic: Inclusive Education & Children with Special Needs
questions.question: A Class VI student explains ideas well orally, but his writing has irregular letter sizes, poor spacing and many spelling errors in spite of great effort. He is most likely to have:
questions.explanation: Dysgraphia is a specific learning disability affecting handwriting, spacing and written expression. Dyscalculia affects number skills, and aphasia is a loss of language ability, usually after brain injury.

questions.topic: Inclusive Education & Children with Special Needs
questions.question: Which is the most appropriate way to meet the needs of a gifted learner in a regular classroom?
options: Give more exercises of the same kind after the regular work is done
Provide enrichment activities and challenging open-ended tasks
Ask the learner to sit quietly after finishing the work
Move the learner to a higher class without assessing other needs
questions.explanation: Gifted learners benefit from enrichment that deepens and extends learning. More of the same work or idle waiting leads to boredom.

questions.question: Many students believe that plants get their food from the soil. A teacher who follows a constructivist approach would treat this idea as:
options: An alternative conception to be used as a starting point for teaching
Evidence that the students are not intelligent
A result of careless reading that needs no attention
A sign that the topic is beyond their developmental stage
questions.explanation: Constructivist teachers elicit children's prior ideas and design experiences that challenge them so that learners reconstruct their understanding (conceptual change).

questions.question:
Assertion (A): Teachers should encourage students to attribute their failures to insufficient effort rather than to low ability.
Reason (R): Attributing failure to a cause that one can control helps learners stay motivated.

Choose the correct option.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
questions.explanation: Effort is an internal, controllable cause, so students who blame effort believe they can improve and keep trying; blaming fixed ability leads to helplessness. Both statements are true and R explains A.

questions.question:
Read the passage and answer.

"For centuries, farmers in the Apatani valley of Arunachal Pradesh have raised fish in their flooded rice fields. The fish feed on insects and weeds, and their droppings enrich the soil, so the farmers need almost no chemical fertiliser or pesticide. Water is guided from forest streams through a network of bamboo channels, and every family takes responsibility for the stretch of channel that passes its fields. Visiting scientists were surprised to find such good harvests from a system that uses so few outside inputs. Today, agricultural experts cite the valley as an example of how traditional knowledge can make farming both productive and sustainable."

According to the passage, the farmers need almost no chemical fertiliser because:
options: The forest streams carry fertile mud into the fields
The bamboo channels add nutrients to the water
Visiting scientists supply them with organic manure
The droppings of the fish enrich the soil
questions.explanation: The passage says the fish's droppings enrich the soil, so the farmers need almost no chemical fertiliser.

questions.question:
Read the passage and answer.

"For centuries, farmers in the Apatani valley of Arunachal Pradesh have raised fish in their flooded rice fields. The fish feed on insects and weeds, and their droppings enrich the soil, so the farmers need almost no chemical fertiliser or pesticide. Water is guided from forest streams through a network of bamboo channels, and every family takes responsibility for the stretch of channel that passes its fields. Visiting scientists were surprised to find such good harvests from a system that uses so few outside inputs. Today, agricultural experts cite the valley as an example of how traditional knowledge can make farming both productive and sustainable."

Which of the following can be inferred from the passage?
options: Modern farming methods have failed everywhere
The Apatani farmers grow only fish
The system depends on cooperation among the families of the valley
Scientists introduced fish farming to the valley
questions.explanation: Each family maintains the stretch of channel passing its fields, so the shared water system works only through cooperation. The other options are not supported.

questions.question:
Read the passage and answer.

"For centuries, farmers in the Apatani valley of Arunachal Pradesh have raised fish in their flooded rice fields. The fish feed on insects and weeds, and their droppings enrich the soil, so the farmers need almost no chemical fertiliser or pesticide. Water is guided from forest streams through a network of bamboo channels, and every family takes responsibility for the stretch of channel that passes its fields. Visiting scientists were surprised to find such good harvests from a system that uses so few outside inputs. Today, agricultural experts cite the valley as an example of how traditional knowledge can make farming both productive and sustainable."

The word 'sustainable' as used in the passage means:
options: Able to continue for a long time without harming the environment
questions.explanation: Sustainable farming can be carried on for a long time without exhausting or damaging natural resources, as the low-input Apatani system shows.

questions.question:
Read the passage and answer.

"For centuries, farmers in the Apatani valley of Arunachal Pradesh have raised fish in their flooded rice fields. The fish feed on insects and weeds, and their droppings enrich the soil, so the farmers need almost no chemical fertiliser or pesticide. Water is guided from forest streams through a network of bamboo channels, and every family takes responsibility for the stretch of channel that passes its fields. Visiting scientists were surprised to find such good harvests from a system that uses so few outside inputs. Today, agricultural experts cite the valley as an example of how traditional knowledge can make farming both productive and sustainable."

In the sentence 'The fish feed on insects and weeds', the word 'feed' is used as a:
questions.explanation: "Feed" tells what the fish do — it is the action word (verb) of the sentence.

questions.question:
Read the stanza and answer.

"I am the river, slow and wide,
I carry the hills to the ocean side;
I hum to the reeds a sleepy tune,
And wear on my back the silver moon."

The river speaks as "I" and is said to hum a tune. The poetic device used here is:
questions.explanation: Giving a river the human abilities to speak and hum is personification.

questions.question:
Read the stanza and answer.

"I am the river, slow and wide,
I carry the hills to the ocean side;
I hum to the reeds a sleepy tune,
And wear on my back the silver moon."

The mood of the stanza is best described as:
questions.explanation: Words such as "slow and wide", "sleepy tune" and "silver moon" create a calm, peaceful mood.

questions.question: According to Stephen Krashen, a learner who feels anxious and is afraid of making mistakes in the English class picks up less language because of a high:
questions.explanation: Krashen's affective filter hypothesis says anxiety, low motivation and low self-confidence act as a mental block that stops input from being acquired.

questions.question: In which method is the learner's mother tongue used extensively to translate texts, and grammar rules are taught explicitly?
questions.explanation: The Grammar-Translation Method relies on translation and explicit grammar rules. The Direct Method avoids the mother tongue, and CLT focuses on meaningful communication.

questions.question: The paragraphs written by many Class VII students lack organisation. The most effective way to help them is to:
options: Give marks only for the final product
Teach process writing — brainstorming, drafting, peer feedback and revising
Ask them to copy model paragraphs from the textbook
Correct every error in red ink
questions.explanation: Process writing treats writing as stages; planning and revising with feedback help learners organise ideas. Copying or heavy correction does not build this skill.

questions.question: Peer assessment of oral presentations in Class VIII, using criteria shared in advance, mainly helps learners to:
options: Reflect on quality and learn from one another
Reduce the need for any teacher feedback
questions.explanation: With shared criteria, peer assessment builds learners' understanding of what good work looks like and supports reflection on their own work.

questions.topic: Challenges of Teaching in Multilingual Classrooms
questions.question: A teacher lets students discuss a science text in their home languages before they write a summary of it in English. This practice:
options: Slows English learning and should be avoided
Is useful only for the weakest learners
Goes against the recommendations of NEP 2020
Uses learners' whole language repertoire to deepen understanding
questions.explanation: Using home languages (translanguaging) helps learners grasp content and then express it in the target language. NCF 2005 and NEP 2020 both encourage using children's languages.

questions.question: Looking quickly through a railway timetable to find the departure time of one particular train is called:
questions.explanation: Scanning is reading quickly to locate a specific piece of information. Skimming is reading quickly for the general idea.

questions.question:
गद्यांश पढ़कर प्रश्न का उत्तर दीजिए।

"विज्ञान ने मनुष्य के जीवन को सरल और सुविधाजनक बनाया है। मोबाइल फ़ोन के द्वारा हम पल भर में दूर बैठे लोगों से बात कर लेते हैं और इंटरनेट से कोई भी जानकारी तुरंत प्राप्त कर लेते हैं। परंतु हर सुविधा के साथ कुछ ज़िम्मेदारियाँ भी आती हैं। तकनीक का अंधाधुंध प्रयोग हमें आलसी बना सकता है और आपसी मेल-जोल को कम कर सकता है। इसलिए आवश्यक है कि हम विवेक से काम लें और तकनीक को अपना साधन बनाएँ, स्वामी नहीं।"

गद्यांश के अनुसार तकनीक के अंधाधुंध प्रयोग से —
options: जानकारी मिलना बंद हो जाता है
मोबाइल फ़ोन महँगे हो जाते हैं
मनुष्य आलसी हो सकता है और आपसी मेल-जोल घट सकता है
विज्ञान की प्रगति रुक जाती है
questions.explanation: गद्यांश में लिखा है कि तकनीक का अंधाधुंध प्रयोग हमें आलसी बना सकता है और आपसी मेल-जोल को कम कर सकता है।

questions.question:
गद्यांश पढ़कर प्रश्न का उत्तर दीजिए।

"विज्ञान ने मनुष्य के जीवन को सरल और सुविधाजनक बनाया है। मोबाइल फ़ोन के द्वारा हम पल भर में दूर बैठे लोगों से बात कर लेते हैं और इंटरनेट से कोई भी जानकारी तुरंत प्राप्त कर लेते हैं। परंतु हर सुविधा के साथ कुछ ज़िम्मेदारियाँ भी आती हैं। तकनीक का अंधाधुंध प्रयोग हमें आलसी बना सकता है और आपसी मेल-जोल को कम कर सकता है। इसलिए आवश्यक है कि हम विवेक से काम लें और तकनीक को अपना साधन बनाएँ, स्वामी नहीं।"

"तकनीक को अपना साधन बनाएँ, स्वामी नहीं" — इस कथन का आशय है —
options: तकनीक का प्रयोग बिल्कुल न करें
तकनीक का प्रयोग आवश्यकता के अनुसार विवेक से करें, उसके अधीन न हों
तकनीक को मालिक की तरह हमें आदेश देने दें
केवल धनी लोग ही तकनीक का प्रयोग करें
questions.explanation: साधन वह है जिसका हम उपयोग करते हैं और स्वामी वह जो हम पर शासन करे। अतः आशय है कि तकनीक हमारे नियंत्रण में रहे, हम उसके गुलाम न बनें।

questions.question:
गद्यांश पढ़कर प्रश्न का उत्तर दीजिए।

"विज्ञान ने मनुष्य के जीवन को सरल और सुविधाजनक बनाया है। मोबाइल फ़ोन के द्वारा हम पल भर में दूर बैठे लोगों से बात कर लेते हैं और इंटरनेट से कोई भी जानकारी तुरंत प्राप्त कर लेते हैं। परंतु हर सुविधा के साथ कुछ ज़िम्मेदारियाँ भी आती हैं। तकनीक का अंधाधुंध प्रयोग हमें आलसी बना सकता है और आपसी मेल-जोल को कम कर सकता है। इसलिए आवश्यक है कि हम विवेक से काम लें और तकनीक को अपना साधन बनाएँ, स्वामी नहीं।"

'सुविधाजनक' शब्द में प्रत्यय है —
questions.explanation: सुविधा + जनक = सुविधाजनक। शब्द के अंत में जुड़कर अर्थ बदलने वाला अंश 'जनक' प्रत्यय है।

questions.question:
गद्यांश पढ़कर प्रश्न का उत्तर दीजिए।

"विज्ञान ने मनुष्य के जीवन को सरल और सुविधाजनक बनाया है। मोबाइल फ़ोन के द्वारा हम पल भर में दूर बैठे लोगों से बात कर लेते हैं और इंटरनेट से कोई भी जानकारी तुरंत प्राप्त कर लेते हैं। परंतु हर सुविधा के साथ कुछ ज़िम्मेदारियाँ भी आती हैं। तकनीक का अंधाधुंध प्रयोग हमें आलसी बना सकता है और आपसी मेल-जोल को कम कर सकता है। इसलिए आवश्यक है कि हम विवेक से काम लें और तकनीक को अपना साधन बनाएँ, स्वामी नहीं।"

गद्यांश में प्रयुक्त 'अंधाधुंध' शब्द का अर्थ है —
questions.explanation: 'अंधाधुंध' का अर्थ है बिना विचार किए, बेहिसाब। गद्यांश में तकनीक के बेहिसाब प्रयोग की बात है।

questions.question: 'यथाशक्ति' में कौन-सा समास है?
questions.explanation: 'यथाशक्ति' (शक्ति के अनुसार) में पहला पद 'यथा' अव्यय है और वही प्रधान है, इसलिए यह अव्ययीभाव समास है।

questions.question: 'आलसी' का विलोम शब्द है —
questions.explanation: 'आलसी' का विलोम 'परिश्रमी' है। निकम्मा, सुस्त और आराम-पसंद इसके समान अर्थ वाले शब्द हैं।

questions.question: भाषा-अर्जन और भाषा-अधिगम में मुख्य अंतर यह है कि —
options: अर्जन औपचारिक कक्षा में होता है, जबकि अधिगम स्वाभाविक परिवेश में
अर्जन स्वाभाविक परिवेश में सहज रूप से होता है, जबकि अधिगम सचेत और औपचारिक प्रयास से होता है
दोनों में कोई अंतर नहीं है
अर्जन केवल लिखने से और अधिगम केवल सुनने से होता है
questions.explanation: भाषा-अर्जन (जैसे मातृभाषा) सहज, अवचेतन रूप से परिवेश में होता है; भाषा-अधिगम नियमों पर ध्यान देकर, सचेत रूप से, प्रायः कक्षा में होता है।

questions.question: उच्च प्राथमिक स्तर पर 'विशेषण' की अवधारणा सिखाने का सबसे उपयुक्त तरीका है —
options: किसी रोचक पाठ में आए शब्दों के प्रयोग से बच्चों को अवधारणा स्वयं खोजने देना
व्याकरण-पुस्तक से अभ्यास की नकल करवाना
उदाहरणों की लंबी सूची याद करवाना
questions.explanation: व्याकरण संदर्भ में और प्रयोग के माध्यम से (उदाहरण से नियम की ओर) सिखाना सबसे प्रभावी है; परिभाषाएँ रटवाने से समझ नहीं बनती।

questions.question: पढ़ने का मुख्य उद्देश्य है —
questions.explanation: पढ़ना अर्थ निर्माण की प्रक्रिया है। उच्चारण, गति और अक्षर-पहचान सहायक हैं, पर मुख्य उद्देश्य अर्थ ग्रहण करना है।

questions.question: कक्षा 7 के बच्चों के लिखित अभिव्यक्ति-कौशल का आकलन करने के लिए सबसे उपयुक्त प्रश्न है —
options: पाठ से पाँच कठिन शब्द छाँटिए।
अपने विद्यालय के वार्षिकोत्सव का वर्णन अपने शब्दों में कीजिए।
questions.explanation: मौलिक वर्णन लिखने में बच्चे को विचारों का संगठन, शब्द-चयन और वाक्य-रचना स्वयं करनी पड़ती है; बाकी प्रश्न स्मरण या पहचान पर आधारित हैं।

questions.question: कक्षा 7 के कई बच्चे लिखते समय 'कि' और 'की' के प्रयोग में गलती करते हैं। सबसे उपयुक्त उपचारात्मक उपाय है —
options: दोनों शब्दों को पचास-पचास बार लिखवाना
सार्थक संदर्भ वाले वाक्यों और पठन-सामग्री के माध्यम से दोनों के प्रयोग पर ध्यान दिलाकर अभ्यास कराना
बच्चों को लिखने से रोक देना
questions.explanation: संदर्भ में प्रयोग देखने और अभ्यास करने से बच्चे अंतर समझते हैं; यांत्रिक लेखन या दंड से समझ विकसित नहीं होती।

questions.question: बहुभाषिक कक्षा में किसी कविता का भाव समझाने के लिए शिक्षिका बच्चों से उनकी अपनी भाषाओं के मिलते-जुलते गीत सुनाने को कहती है। यह —
options: बच्चों की भाषाओं को संसाधन के रूप में उपयोग करना है
questions.explanation: बच्चों की भाषाओं को कक्षा में स्थान देना उनके अनुभव को सीखने से जोड़ता है; NCF 2005 बहुभाषिकता को संसाधन मानती है।

questions.question: What is the LCM of 18, 24 and 30?
What is the smallest number by which 1800 must be multiplied to make it a perfect square?
questions.explanation: 1800 = 2³ × 3² × 5². Only the factor 2 has an odd power, so multiplying by 2 gives 2⁴ × 3² × 5² = 3600 = 60².

questions.question: The sum of three consecutive even numbers is 78. What is the largest of them?
questions.explanation: Let the numbers be x, x + 2, x + 4. Then 3x + 6 = 78, so x = 24. The largest is 28.

questions.question: A sum of money at simple interest amounts to ₹5,600 in 2 years and to ₹6,200 in 4 years. What is the rate of interest per annum?
questions.explanation: Interest for 2 years = 6200 − 5600 = ₹600, so ₹300 per year. Principal = 5600 − 600 = ₹5,000. Rate = 300 × 100 / 5000 = 6%.

questions.question: Two parallel lines are cut by a transversal. If one of the interior angles on the same side of the transversal is 72°, the other interior angle on that side is:
questions.explanation: Co-interior angles on the same side of a transversal are supplementary: 180° − 72° = 108°.

questions.question: An exterior angle of a triangle is 110°, and one of its interior opposite angles is 45°. The other interior opposite angle is:
questions.explanation: An exterior angle equals the sum of the two interior opposite angles: 110° − 45° = 65°.

questions.question: The diagonals of a rhombus are 16 cm and 12 cm. What is its area?
questions.explanation: Area of a rhombus = ½ × d₁ × d₂ = ½ × 16 × 12 = 96 cm².

questions.question: How many bricks, each measuring 25 cm × 12.5 cm × 7.5 cm, are needed to build a wall 6 m long, 3 m high and 25 cm thick?
The mean of 8, 12, x, 15 and 20 is 13. What is the median of the data?
questions.explanation: Sum = 13 × 5 = 65, so x = 65 − 55 = 10. Arranged: 8, 10, 12, 15, 20. The median is the middle value, 12.

questions.question: Which activity best connects school mathematics with the community?
options: Students solve all the exercises at the end of the chapter
Students memorise the formulas for percentage
Students survey local shops to compare prices and work out discounts
Students copy solved examples from the board
questions.explanation: A local price survey uses real data from children's surroundings, linking percentage and discount to everyday life.

questions.question: A student writes (a + b)² = a² + b². Which remedial strategy is most effective?
options: Make the student write the correct identity twenty times
Use an area model — a square of side (a + b) divided into parts — to show the missing 2ab
Tell the student the answer is wrong and move on
Give many more problems of the same type without feedback
questions.explanation: The area model lets the student see that the square of side (a + b) contains a², b² and two rectangles of area ab, which builds conceptual understanding of the identity.

questions.question: Which practice is most likely to reduce mathematics anxiety among students?
options: Valuing different solution strategies and treating mistakes as part of learning
Frequent timed tests with marks displayed publicly
Punishing wrong answers so that students become careful
Insisting on one standard method for every problem
questions.explanation: Anxiety falls when the classroom is safe for trying, erring and explaining varied approaches. Public comparison, punishment and rigid methods raise anxiety.

questions.question: Deficiency of which vitamin causes scurvy, with symptoms such as bleeding gums?
questions.explanation: Scurvy is caused by lack of vitamin C. Vitamin A deficiency causes night blindness, vitamin D rickets and vitamin B1 beriberi.

questions.question: An ant's sting injects an acid into the skin. Which of the following is the most suitable thing to rub on the affected area?
questions.explanation: The sting contains formic acid. A mild base such as baking soda neutralises it. Vinegar and lemon juice are acids, and salt solution is neutral.

questions.question: Which metal is stored in kerosene because it reacts vigorously with air and water?
questions.explanation: Sodium is highly reactive and can catch fire in air, so it is kept under kerosene. Phosphorus, a non-metal, is stored in water.

questions.question: In human beings, digestion of food is completed and the digested food is mainly absorbed in the:
questions.explanation: Digestion of carbohydrates, proteins and fats is completed in the small intestine, and its villi absorb the digested food. The large intestine mainly absorbs water and salts.

questions.question: Which microorganism is used to make bread dough rise?
questions.explanation: Yeast respires and releases carbon dioxide, which makes the dough rise. Lactobacillus sets curd, Rhizobium fixes nitrogen, and Penicillium gives penicillin.

questions.question: A force of 200 N acts on an area of 0.5 m². What is the pressure exerted?
questions.explanation: Pressure = force ÷ area = 200 N ÷ 0.5 m² = 400 N/m² = 400 Pa.

questions.question: If the number of turns of wire in an electromagnet is increased while the current stays the same, its strength:
questions.explanation: The magnetic field of an electromagnet is stronger with more turns of wire (and with more current).

questions.question: Sound cannot travel through:
questions.explanation: Sound needs a medium (solid, liquid or gas) to travel. It cannot pass through a vacuum.

questions.question: Which of the following was formed from the remains of dead plants buried deep under the earth millions of years ago?
questions.explanation: Coal formed from buried forests under heat and pressure (carbonisation). NCERT explains that petroleum formed from organisms living in the sea, and iron ore and limestone are not fossil fuels.

questions.question: According to NCF 2005, "cognitive validity" of the science curriculum requires that:
options: Content reflects the latest research findings
Content, process, language and activities match the age and cognitive reach of the child
Science teaching conveys values such as honesty and objectivity
Science is linked with its history and with society
questions.explanation: Cognitive validity concerns age-appropriateness. Content validity is about correct and significant content, ethical validity about values, and historical validity about the history of science.

questions.question: A teacher asks students to predict whether a candle covered by an inverted glass will keep burning, then lets them test it and explain what they observe. This approach is best described as:
questions.explanation: Predicting, testing and explaining is an inquiry-based (POE) strategy in which students build understanding from their own observations.

questions.question: Making a simple stethoscope in class from a funnel, a rubber tube and a balloon is an example of:
questions.explanation: Improvised apparatus made from everyday materials is a low-cost, innovative teaching aid encouraged by NCERT for science.

pyqBlueprint.method: Compiled from the CTET papers of August 2023, January 2024, July 2024 and December 2024 (official question booklets/answer keys as reproduced on coaching sites) and memory-based shift analyses of the February 2026 cycle (no CTET was held in calendar 2025). WebSearch was used for the 2024–2026 analyses (PW, Careers360, Adda247, Prepp); full official papers could not be fetched, so the archetype list also draws on the writer's own knowledge of earlier CTET papers. Patterns are described in our own words; no real question is reproduced. Frequencies are per 30-question section.

archetypes.pattern: Scenario → principle of development (cephalocaudal, proximodistal, general-to-specific, continuity, individual differences, interrelated domains)
"Which statement about development is NOT correct" — stages of childhood/adolescence, development as qualitative and quantitative, lifelong
Nature–nurture: choose the correct statement about the interaction of heredity and environment
Agents of socialisation (family as primary, school/peers/media as secondary) and the teacher's role in socialisation
Child's behaviour → Piagetian stage feature (animism, egocentrism, centration, conservation, object permanence, hypothetico-deductive reasoning)
Piaget's processes: schema, assimilation, accommodation, equilibration identified from an example; distractors swap assimilation/accommodation
Vygotsky: ZPD, scaffolding, more knowledgeable other, private speech, cultural tools — concept from a classroom description
A child's moral reasoning statement → Kohlberg level/stage (punishment-obedience, instrumental, good boy–good girl, law and order, social contract)
Compare/critique the theorists (Piaget vs Vygotsky on language and learning, Gilligan's critique of Kohlberg) — pick the correct statement
Features of child-centred/progressive education and the teacher as facilitator (Dewey, NCF 2005)
Gardner's multiple intelligences from a child's profile; Sternberg's triarchic components; IQ basics
Relationship of language and thought: Vygotsky vs Piaget, Chomsky's LAD, private speech
Gender stereotypes in school practices/textbooks and the teacher's appropriate response; gender as a social construct
Individual differences: sources of diversity and how to address diverse learners (differentiated instruction)
Distinguish assessment of / for / as learning; purpose of CCE and formative vs summative assessment
Assessment tools and NEP 2020 ideas: portfolio, rubrics, open-ended questions, holistic progress card, competency-based assessment

archetypes.topic: Inclusive Education & Children with Special Needs
archetypes.pattern: Symptoms → learning disability/disorder (dyslexia, dysgraphia, dyscalculia, dyspraxia, ADHD, autism)

archetypes.topic: Inclusive Education & Children with Special Needs
archetypes.pattern: Best inclusive practice for a child with a specific disability (visual, hearing, locomotor); RPwD Act 2016 facts; universal design

archetypes.topic: Inclusive Education & Children with Special Needs
archetypes.pattern: Strategies for gifted/creative children and learners from disadvantaged groups (enrichment, divergent tasks, avoiding labelling)
Constructivist view of learning: children's errors and misconceptions as windows into thinking; often in Assertion–Reason format
Motivation: intrinsic vs extrinsic, attribution of success/failure, mastery vs performance goals
Cognition and learning: metacognition, factors affecting learning, emotions and learning, how children think
Factual detail/reason stated in a 150–250-word prose passage; distractors use words from the passage with wrong links
Inference, "NOT supported by the passage" or central idea; trap = option true in general but not stated
Vocabulary in context: synonym/antonym of a word as used in the passage
Grammar item from the passage: part of speech, sentence type, tense/voice, phrase/clause
Literal meaning of a line/stanza of an unseen poem; "which does the poet NOT say"
Poetic device in a quoted line (metaphor, simile, personification, alliteration) or rhyme scheme
Tone/theme of the poem or meaning of a poetic word
Theorists of acquisition (Krashen's input/affective filter, Chomsky's LAD, Vygotsky) and acquisition vs learning; errors as part of learning
Identify a method/approach from a description (whole language, CLT, TPR, direct, grammar-translation, structural)
Best activity to develop listening or speaking at a given class level (role play, storytelling, listening for information)
Name the language sub-skill described (skimming, scanning, intensive vs extensive listening/reading)
Remedial step for a reading/writing difficulty, or choice of authentic/supplementary materials
What a given tool assesses or the best way to assess a skill (cloze, rubric, portfolio, oral tasks)

archetypes.topic: Challenges of Teaching in Multilingual Classrooms
archetypes.pattern: Multilingualism as a resource, use of home language, language across the curriculum

पर्यायवाची/विलोम शब्द, "जो पर्यायवाची नहीं है" प्रारूप
बच्चों की भाषायी त्रुटियाँ, घर की भाषा और भाषा-अर्जन के प्रति शिक्षक का दृष्टिकोण

विशिष्ट भाषायी कठिनाई (ध्वनि-भ्रम, वर्तनी) के लिए उपचारात्मक शिक्षण
बहुभाषिकता को संसाधन मानना, बच्चों की मातृभाषा का कक्षा में उपयोग
HCF/LCM of 2–3 numbers, divisibility and primes (Class VI–VII level); distractors = product or partial LCM
Integers, rational numbers, exponents, squares/square roots and cubes — e.g. smallest multiplier for a perfect square
Linear equation in one variable or its word problem (consecutive numbers, ages)
Ratio–proportion, percentage, profit–loss, simple interest from two amounts
Algebraic expressions and identities, factorisation, value of an expression
Angles: parallel lines and transversal, polygon interior/exterior angles, angle ratios in a triangle
3-D shapes (Euler's formula, faces/edges/vertices), symmetry and properties of quadrilaterals
Triangle properties: exterior-angle property, Pythagoras, congruence criteria
Area of trapezium, rhombus, parallelogram or circle from given measures

Mean/median/mode of raw data (often with one unknown value), pie-chart angle, simple probability
Deductive vs inductive reasoning, axioms/postulates, van Hiele level from a student's geometric statement
